videos.script:
This course is about speed. How fast a page shows something, how fast it answers a tap, and whether it still works when the network goes. {{where}} It starts with one question that decides most of the rest. Where is the page's HTML made? In the browser, by your JavaScript, or on a server, before anything is sent?

{{planner}} You will answer it with a real app. A small study planner, written in plain TypeScript and built with Vite. You will build it in this lesson, and every lesson after this one measures it or changes it.

{{two}} Then you will serve it two ways. First as most single-page apps are served: an empty page and a script that fills it. Then from a small Node server that draws each page before sending it. {{nojs}} You will open both in Chromium with JavaScript switched off, and see what a crawler sees.

{{slow}} And you will slow the network down on purpose. Three hundred milliseconds on every request. The difference between the two ways stops being theory.

{{choose}} By the end you will know what each way costs, and how to choose between them for one page at a time.
